patients.summary: Graduate student who joined the practice at 24 in 2019 with a past college depressive episode. Schizoaffective disorder, depressive type is diagnosed by psychiatry in 2022, then body dysmorphic disorder; sertraline from late 2022. Two ED visits for suicidal ideation (2025, 2026) each lead to an inpatient psychiatric stay; paliperidone is added in 2026.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is moving here this month to start a graduate program and wants a primary care doctor nearby. Private insurance card info taken. No urgent issues. Booked new patient appt 8/20 at 9:00. Asked her to bring any old records or the name of her last office so we can request them.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
24-year-old woman, new to the area, here to set up primary care. Starting a graduate program this fall. Feels well, no complaints today.

PMH: one episode of depression in college (2016). Saw the campus counselor weekly for most of a semester, never took medication, and says it lifted by that summer. No symptoms since. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: mother has major depression; one maternal aunt with bipolar disorder; one maternal uncle with schizophrenia. No early heart disease or cancers she knows of.
Social: grad student, lives with a roommate. Never smoked, does not drink, no drug use. Walks a lot.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap 2017 at her old office, normal per pt.

ROS negative across systems. Mood good. Sleep fine.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant, good eye contact. HEENT normal, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin clear. Neuro grossly intact. Affect bright and appropriate.

PHQ-9: 3.

Plan:
- Records release signed for her prior office.
- One-time HIV and hep C screen drawn today.
- Flu shot when it arrives in October, nurse visit.
- Pap due next year; can do at a physical in the winter.
- Talked through the family psych history; she knows to reach out early if her mood dips again.
RTC for physical in about 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Paige, both screening tests (HIV and hepatitis C) came back negative. Nothing more needed. Nice meeting you this week.

reports.text: Specimen adequate for evaluation. Endocervical/transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed records (14 pages) from patient's previous family medicine office, covering 2012 to 2018. Includes immunization record and 2017 Pap. Abstracted: HPV x3 2007-2008, Tdap 8/2015, Pap 4/2017 NILM. Office notes are routine well visits and a sprained wrist in 2013. Counseling for low mood in 2016 was through her college, not this office. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed old records. Immunizations entered. Pap 2017 normal, next due 2020. Nothing else to act on.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine given L deltoid, lot recorded. No prior reactions. Tolerated well, waited in clinic a few minutes, no problems.

reports.text: Specimen adequate. Transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. No organisms identified.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. First semester went well, a lot of reading, a lab job on campus. Sleeping 7 hours. Mood good, no recurrence of the college depression. No new meds. Still not smoking or drinking.

Exam: well, NAD. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses. Abdomen benign. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap collected. Skin normal. Mood and affect normal.

PHQ-9 2.

A/P: healthy 24F.
- Pap today (last 2017).
- Flu done this season. Immunizations otherwise current.
- Next physical in a year.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap smear was normal. Next one in three years.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Masked, screened at door, no COVID symptoms or exposures. Flu vaccine R deltoid. Tolerated without issue.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for yearly. Classes remote most of this year, which she finds isolating, but she says she is managing. Has a COVID vaccine appointment at a pharmacy next month. No health complaints.

Exam: unremarkable. Heart and lungs normal, abdomen soft, no thyroid enlargement, skin clear. Calm, organized, appropriate.

PHQ-9 4, mostly tiredness and some trouble concentrating.

Plan: routine. Encouraged getting outside and keeping a schedule while remote. Pap not due until 2023. COVID vaccine as planned. Physical again in about a year; she'd prefer December after the semester.

documents.title: Pharmacy COVID vaccine record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt sent a photo of her vaccine card through the portal. Pfizer dose 1 4/9/21, dose 2 4/30/21, both at a retail pharmacy. Entered into immunization history and state registry checked, matches.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid. Quiet today, said she was tired from the semester. Reminded her of the physical booked in December.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No show for 1:40 physical. Called cell, went to voicemail, left message to call back and reschedule.

documents.title: Reschedule your physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Paige, we missed you in December. Please call or reply here to book your yearly physical when it works for you.
